subject: Integration gate cadence and traffic ownership plan
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmefinance.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Victor Chen <victor.chen@acmefinance.com>, Acme Finance Legal <legal@acmefinance.com>
Date: 2027-05-07T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Integration gate cadence and ownership questions

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and engineering asked if you can provide a concise integration gate schedule we can include in the SOW. Specifically we need:

- A 6–8 week timeline with high-level gates (sandbox, pilot, canary, full traffic)
- Responsibilities for integration tasks (who at Redwood vs. Acme)
- Expected downtime or traffic diversion windows and rollback criteria
- Any pre-requisites we should list for security sign-off (SOCs, audit logs, PKI exchange)

Can you return a short schedule and ownership matrix by end of week? Attaching the RFP template for context.

Thanks —
Olivia Barnes
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Financial Services

Attachment: ACME-RFP-Integration-Template.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmefinance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration gate cadence and ownership questions

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clarity. Drafted a compact plan below (6-week pilot-to-production option). Attaching an ownership matrix and a traffic-shift cadence PDF. This is intentionally conservative; we can compress or extend gates depending on your change windows and compliance sign-offs.

Summary (proposed):
Week 0–1: Sandbox integration
  - Redwood: provide sandbox env, key exchange (KMS stub), sample dataset, API access tokens
  - Acme: validate connectivity, run representative queries, share security contact for SOC/Q&A

Week 2–3: Pilot (closed group)
  - Redwood: deploy pilot model variant, enable KV caching and logging, telemetry hooks to your SIEM
  - Acme: route a 1–5% traffic slice via feature flag, run acceptance tests against eval prompts
  - Gate: meet performance and quality SLAs in pilot (latency p95 < 250ms, degradation delta < 3% on eval set)

Week 4: Canary (gradual ramp)
  - Redwood: orchestrate progressive ramp (5% -> 25%) with automated rollback triggers and alerting
  - Acme: monitor business KPIs and provide go/no-go within 24h windows

Week 5: Full production (cutover)
  - Redwood: handover runbook and escalate contacts; enable dedicated capacity if contracted
  - Acme: switch traffic, validate data retention and audit log visibility

Rollback criteria (examples):
- Sustained error rate > 0.5% over 5m or latency p95 > 400ms
- Quality regression on core prompt set > 5% per eval metrics

Pre-reqs for security sign-off:
- SOC 2 Type II report (we will provide recent report)
- IP allowlist entries and mTLS cert exchange
- KMS integration plan (we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys)

Attachments: redwood-integration-ownership-matrix.xlsx, traffic-shift-cadence.pdf, draft-sow-acme.docx

Next steps: I propose a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through ownership rows and confirm your acceptance criteria. If that works, Marissa will send a calendar invite.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-07T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration gate cadence and ownership questions

Looping in Grace for CS/telemetry ownership and Aditya for infra sizing. A couple of internal notes before the call:

- Sandbox access: we should deliver a pre-seeded sandbox (token + sample kv cache snapshot) rather than asking the customer to seed data. Reduces friction.
- Pilot eval set: Grace — can you prepare a 25-example prompt set and define pass/fail thresholds for the pilot gate?
- Dedicated capacity: Aditya — if customer wants dedicated GPU pools at cutover, we need number-of-concurrent-requests estimates ASAP; otherwise propose shared hosted with reserved throughput.

I’ll draft the calendar invite with the link to the ownership matrix so they can comment inline.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-07T13:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration gate cadence and ownership questions

Thanks — I will:
- Build the 25-prompt pilot eval and mark categories (latency, factuality, hallucination, instruction-following).
- Provide an acceptance dashboard template (shared Drive link in the invite).
- Include an activity list for telemetry (what logs we emit, retention windows, sampling).

Also recommended to include a short runbook snippet in the pilot phase that shows how to trigger a rollback via feature flag and the contact escalation chain. I’ll add that to the matrix.

- Grace
Manager, Customer Success
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmefinance.com>, Victor Chen <victor.chen@acmefinance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-08T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration gate cadence and ownership questions

Hi Olivia / Victor —

Updated materials attached based on internal alignment:
- redwood-integration-ownership-matrix.xlsx (owners + who does what by gate)
- traffic-shift-cadence.pdf (ramp plan with rollback windows)
- draft-sow-acme.docx (SOW section drafts you can paste into your template)

Quick highlights/changes from initial note:
- We will seed a sandbox snapshot and provide a short script to populate KV cache for performance parity.
- Pilot acceptance includes an automated eval job run daily; results pushed to your Drive link and a webhook for real-time alerts.
- Canary ramp will use progressive percentages + automated circuit-breaker tied to p95 latency and error rates.

Proposed meeting: 2027-05-08 15:00 PT (30m) — calendar invite to follow. Please tell us if legal needs earlier visibility to the SOW draft and we’ll share a redlineable doc.

Best regards,
Rishi
From: Victor Chen <victor.chen@acmefinance.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmefinance.com>, Acme Finance Legal <legal@acmefinance.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-10T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration gate cadence and ownership questions

Rishi —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the ownership matrix. Legal would like the SOW docx sent directly to legal@acmefinance.com for redlines; they will target comments by EOD Friday. A couple of quick clarifications from engineering:

- For the sandbox snapshot, can you confirm whether PII is scrubbed by default? If not, we need a sanitized dataset and details of the scrub process.
- For the canary automated evals: can we add a secondary webhook for our internal ops so we get immediate paging on circuit-breaker triggers?

If you can confirm those two items in writing, we’ll be comfortable moving to the pilot gate next week.

Thanks —
Victor Chen
VP, Engineering
Acme Financial Services
